newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A volatile afternoon on the currency market saw the rand jump to its best level since December 4 on strong offshore dollar sales, only to reverse gains before the official close as players took profits at the lower levels, forex traders said.
The rand ended at 4.6670/6720 on the dollar from an afternoon best bid of 4.6440 and from 4.6685/6735 late on Wednesday.
"Offshore guys sold dollars which caught the locals long...basically the guys were bailing long dollar positions," a senior currency trader said.
"It's amazing...from a high of around 4.6450 we came all the way back to around previous closing levels within about an hour," he added.
Traders said the rand initially drifted higher on the back of a worse-than-expected December reserves figure at 10.305 billion rand from November's 10.93 billion rand.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast December reserves at 10.85 billion rand, with the range 10.4 to 11.2 billion rand.
The currency then drifted around the 4.68 level during the mid morning session before jumping to its strongest level in five weeks in the afternoon.
Traders expected a further test of the downside on Friday, possibly to around the 4.64 area.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 7.9002/9110 on sterling from 7.8685/8816 late on Wednesday and at 0.3368/3374 on the mark from 0.3365/3370 previously.
South African bonds had another positive day marked by good local institutional buying.
The key R150 stock was last trading at 15.90 percent from 15.89 percent late on Wednesday.
"It was an enormous fight between the bulls and the bears and in the end the bulls won more ground," a trader said.
Bonds started weaker on the lower reserves figure and weaker U.S. Treasuries but strengthened in the afternoon on the rand's gains and better U.S. Treasuries following the release of U.S. PPI data.
Dealers said the outlook was bullish and they expected the market to follow the currency closely on Friday.
Next week, direction on the money market would be key in dictating the trend, some noted.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net buyers of 217.44 million rand of South African bonds on Wednesday after a net selling position of 52.38 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative turnover was 4.12 billion rand on Wednesday from 6.01 billion rand on Tuesday, the exchange said.
On the money market, the daily money market shortage fell to 9.444 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.686 billion rand on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said.
Three-month NCD rates were steady at between 17.35 and 17.65 percent while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 16.65 and 16.95 percent.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
